Subject: Private Offer: timeboxed promotional discount + reseller net cascade

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, Helios is evaluating a 12‑month private offer on Azure with a 15% promotional discount for the first 3 months to accelerate onboarding. Two quick asks so we can draft a clean private offer and procurement packet:

1) Confirm whether your reseller (BrightWave) needs the promo to flow-through as a guaranteed minimum net or can accept a timeboxed uplift (i.e., promo applies to customer invoice but reseller receives standard pass‑through plus a one‑time onboarding fee).
2) Any constraints on invoice timing (month-end vs. net30) and whether your finance team requires an explicit reseller waterfall in the PO?

I attached a rough pricing worksheet and a diagram of a suggested reseller net cascade for reference (draft_pricing.xlsx, reseller_net_cascade_v1.png).

If you want, we can turn this into two discrete line items in the private offer: (A) base reserved capacity (node hours) at net price, (B) promotional credit applied as invoice credit for first three months. That usually keeps marketplace listing simpler while preserving a measurable reseller net.

I'll loop Ben on the margin mechanics; Irene will advise on procurement flow. Proposed next step: short call Monday to confirm flow and any legal doc needs. Does 10am PT Monday work?

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com
Attachments: 2025-06-27-draft_pricing.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB); reseller_net_cascade_v1.png (png, 48KB)

Subject: Re: Private Offer: timeboxed promotional discount + reseller net cascade

Neha —

Appreciate the note and the attachments. Quick answers:

- BrightWave prefers a firm reseller net (they build their margin into forecasting). If the promo reduces their visible gross, they want a guaranteed addback (one of: guaranteed onboarding fee of $X, or a stepped passback for months 1–3). They dislike promo-only invoice credits that appear after close.
- Procurement prefers invoice timing at month-end and Net30. They also asked we provide an explicit waterfall so they can map to BrightWave’s ledger.

We are open to the two-line approach — just need the reseller addition to appear in the PO (line item or appendix).

10am PT Monday works for a short sync.

Best,
Alex Miller
Head of Cloud Engineering, Helios Labs
alex.miller@helioslabs.io

Alex / Neha —

Thanks for the clarity, Alex. Attaching a simple waterfall and two alternative structures so you can show BrightWave finance:

Option A — Guaranteed reseller addback: Redwood includes a fixed reseller fee (one-time onboarding credit) of $35k that appears on the PO as a separate line. Customer sees a 15% invoice promo for months 1–3; BrightWave receives the $35k addback regardless of invoiced promo. Pros: predictable reseller margin; cons: small accounting uplift on our side.

Option B — Stepped passback: Promo reduces invoice; we pass through a monthly cashback to BrightWave for months 1–3 at 50% of the promo delta. Pros: aligns incentives; cons: more complex monthly reconciliation.

Operational notes:
- We can create the private offer listing for Azure with two line items: (1) Reserved node hours (committed price), (2) One-time reseller_onboarding_credit (negative line item). Azure marketplace permits negative credits if documented in the PO appendix.
- For Helios procurement, we'll include an appendix with the reseller waterfall (clear mapping: invoice promo, reseller gross, passback/addback mechanics). That appendix is the simplest way to keep the marketplace catalog entry clean while satisfying BrightWave finance.

Attachments referenced: Helios_PO_template.docx (PO skeleton with appendix placeholders), reseller_net_cascade_v1.png (annotated), 2025-06-27-draft_pricing.xlsx (pricing scenarios).

Neha — I can join Monday’s call to run through the two examples and comment on tax/withholding implications in the US.

—Ben
